title: Estimation of covariance matrix for Stokes-like measurement under phase-space deformation
abstract: We investigate the signatures of phase-space noncommutativity in an anisotropic oscillator and propose an optomechanical protocol to experimentally characterize it through Stokes-like measurements of an optical field. Starting from a deformed phase-space algebra characterized by the position-position and momentum-momentum noncommutativity parameters $θ$ and $η$, we employ the Darboux transformation to construct an equivalent Hamiltonian in canonical variables. The resulting effective dynamics exhibits correlations between the oscillator degrees of freedom. We derive the corresponding covariance matrix and examine how the noncommutative parameters enter the mechanical dynamics and the optical response.   By coupling the oscillator to a coherent optical probe, we obtain analytical expressions for the time-dependent optical coherence attenuation and the nonlinear Kerr phase. We then formulate an interferometric detection scheme through Stokes-like measurements, in which the outgoing optical field is combined with a phase-controlled reference beam at a balanced beam splitter, and the resulting photocurrents are measured using photodetectors. The optical response provides access to the modified normal-mode frequencies, which enables us to estimate experimental values of $θ$ and $η$. Our results establish a theoretical connection between NC-space dynamics, Gaussian-state correlations, and experimentally accessible optical observables, suggesting an optomechanical route toward testing signatures of phase-space noncommutativity.
summary: This paper proposes an experimental method to detect phase-space noncommutativity in an oscillator by coupling it to an optical cavity. By performing Stokes-like measurements on the output light, the authors can extract modified normal-mode frequencies. These frequencies are then used to estimate the noncommutative parameters ($	heta$ and $\eta$), establishing a novel optomechanical test for non-canonical quantum dynamics.
main_problem: The paper investigates how phase-space noncommutativity in an anisotropic oscillator can be experimentally detected using an optomechanical setup.
main_result: The optical response, measured via Stokes-like interferometry, provides a theoretical link to estimate the noncommutative parameters ($	heta$ and $\eta$) by determining the modified normal-mode frequencies.
method: The authors derive the covariance matrix for the output optical field and formulate an interferometric detection scheme using phase-controlled reference beams.
model_or_system: The system involves an anisotropic oscillator whose dynamics are governed by a noncommutative phase-space algebra, coupled to a coherent optical probe in an optomechanical interaction.
key_observables: Optical coherence attenuation ($A_M$), nonlinear Kerr phase ($\Phi_K$), and the estimated covariance matrix for the output field.
important_parameters: Noncommutative parameters ($	heta$ and $\eta$), mechanical normal-mode frequencies ($\lambda_j$), and coupling strengths ($g$).
main_assumptions: The mechanical oscillator state is approximated by a Gaussian state (low temperature, below 4 Kelvin), and the measurement relies on an ideal optomechanical interaction.
paper_structure: The paper moves from establishing the noncommutative Hamiltonian and its transformation to canonical variables, deriving the covariance matrix, and finally applying this framework to an optomechanical measurement protocol using Stokes-like measurements to extract the deformation parameters.
why_interesting: This work bridges abstract mathematical concepts (noncommutative geometry) with concrete, measurable quantum optics experiments (optomechanics), providing a tangible pathway to test fundamental physics beyond standard quantum mechanics.
